definition: For this comparison, a real common nature taken as a substantial constituent shared by individuals, rather than the numerically singular mental or vocal sign used for them. This describes the target of the relevant Ockham objections, not all realist theories.
note: Contrast interface for the reported extramental-common-nature dispute in Summa logicae I.15–17. A separate Platonic exemplar and an individual substantial form are not identified with this proposed common constituent. A universal argument against every realism would need additional defended bridges.
